modules.name: Vista audit, node contract and frame rule
modules.design_question: Which Vista parts become the View-and-Warn node, what typed ports does it expose, and in which frame does each calculation run?
modules.method: Vista v09.16 is one WebGL2 page: explorer.js (218 KB, 161 functions, one global state), report.js, pdf.js, six self-test scripts. KEEP: polygon-clip kernels, result precedence and no-compliance wording guards, fixtures F1-F3, hash state, PDF writer, cone-fit camera rule. REFACTOR: split explorer.js into assets, picking, camera and ui modules; typed functions replace the global state and the /api/check shim; checks run in a Worker; self-tests run headless. REPLACE: the 38.7 MB triangle context, apex-only origins, the flat ceiling as main test, per-part bounding boxes, the duplicate cone copy in Form Studio, and the Vista equirectangular frame (0.20% short east-west, 0.58% north-south, 25.7 m short on QE to Barclay). FRAME RULE: containment and clipping run only in the EPSG:3157 grid (cones, parcel and design all projected; edges straight in the grid); distances, azimuths and Dx are reported only from GeographicLib on GRS80; a grid bearing is never compared with a geodesic azimuth; z stays orthometric in the datum of the limit, and an ENU up axis is never used for exceedance. Every output carries units, CRS, vertical datum, dataset versions and an estimate flag. Vertical datum UNKNOWN: viewing works, numbers are blocked. Add MIT or Apache-2.0 licences and an ODbL and OGL-Vancouver NOTICE.
inputs: ConeSet: per view id, origin lat/lon/z with quality level and horizontal datum, plan polygon, limit hypotheses H0 flat or H1 sloped with tier and reference building, status, amendment years, portal modified stamp
TerrainSampler: z(x,y), vertical datum, sigma, source tile ids
ContextTiles: LOD1 buildings with height source, epoch and datums
DesignMassing: placed triangle meshes, layers, units, horizontal and vertical datum (vertical may be UNKNOWN)
ViewpointSet: protected origins, rooftop picks, user points
ZoningLimit: optional by-law or ODP maximum height typed by the designer (open data has no height field)
SiteSpec: City parcel polygon, or a hypothetical block in local coordinates with placed or unplaced status
outputs: ExceedanceReport per cone and governing cone: e, U95, dominant term, worst point, state, clause ids, estimate flag (renamed from ViolationReport)
HeadroomMap: governing limit minus grade per cell, with a state code
ViewRender: existing and proposed images with overlays
SkylineProfile: elevation angle against azimuth
PdfReport
Provenance: dataset versions, hashes, assumptions

modules.name: Protected-viewpoint camera rig
modules.design_question: How do we render the design from each protected origin with correct position, eye height and a field of view matched to the cone?
modules.method: Origin: City survey coordinates and geodetic elevation when obtained (quality Q2); otherwise the polygon apex (Q0, labelled estimated; the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m). Open-data text for 9.1 and 9.2 names the Walking Figures plaza but the 2026 Table 1 extract names the City Hall stairs. Eye z = ground z + eye height (default 1.6 m, editable; no City value found). Ground z: LiDAR-2022 DTM (portal: 0.081 m at 95%, land cover not stated); piers, bridges and seawalls (G1, G2, E, K) use first returns plus a structure offset. Heading = bisector of the boundary azimuths. Presets: cone-fit (Vista rule hfov = clamp(1.5 x spread + 8, 24, 100)); standard 39.6 deg human view; cylindrical strip when hfov exceeds 60 deg (only view 27.2). Depth: reversed-Z when EXT_clip_control exists, else logarithmic depth; store the path on the camera record; near 1-2 m, far at least 60 km. Haze per preset: evidence captures use none; the Vista context fog (9,000 m) is removed. The render applies the same apparent-drop function as the profile (M05). Subject-visible test checks silhouette-to-sky contrast, not depth alone. Overlay boundaries, limit-plane footprint, quality badge. Calibrate once per view against a site photo.

TerrainSampler ground z at the origin (LiDAR DTM, DSM on structures)
Structure-offset table for piers, decks and seawalls
ContextTiles and DesignMassing for rendering
Eye height, preset and haze choice
outputs: ViewRender per cone: existing and proposed, with boundary and limit-plane overlays
Camera record: lat, lon, z, eye height, yaw, pitch, hfov, vfov, aspect, projection, depth path, haze preset, origin quality
Landmark calibration residual in degrees

parameters.name: eye_z
parameters.relationship: ground_z + h_eye; h_eye default 1.6 m (Vista), user editable; no City eye height found (a 5 ft 6 in average-person reference appears only in a 2023 City Q and A snippet).

parameters.name: hfov_fit
parameters.relationship: clamp(1.5 x spread + 8, 24, 100); spread 1.61 to 53.0 deg; 14 of 24 views sit at the 24 deg floor; rule only in report.js. Vista pitch = clamp(max(0.12 vfov, top angle - 0.32 vfov), -2, 28 deg).

parameters.name: pitch_fit
parameters.relationship: Aim between the elevation angles to the limit plane at the near and far edges, atan((L - z_eye)/D), plus 3 deg margin; neutral default 0 deg while L is unknown.

parameters.name: far_plane
parameters.relationship: At least 60 km with reversed-Z or log depth; the Vista observer far plane is 45,000 m; subjects are 12.5-24.6 km from the 17 distinct origins.

parameters.name: haze
parameters.relationship: Vista context fog far is 9,000 m (55% blend cap); backdrop pass 42,000 m gives 4.9% haze at 12.5 km, 18.9% at 24.6 km (default style). Evidence preset: no fog. Atmosphere preset: user visibility, blend capped at 25% (team choice).

parameters.name: depth_path
parameters.relationship: Reversed-Z needs EXT_clip_control (Khronos: Community Approved 2023-11-02; no browser support list). Detect with getExtension at runtime, else logarithmic depth; record the path on the camera record.

parameters.name: render_curvature
parameters.relationship: Every vertex drops by (1 - k) d^2/(2R), k = 0.13, d = horizontal distance from the camera, for terrain, context and the limit overlay; numbers e, L and U never use it; the profile uses the same function.

parameters.name: panorama_preset
parameters.relationship: Rectilinear edge stretch is 1/cos^2(hfov/2): 1.92 at 87.5 deg (view 27.2), 1.24 at 51.8 deg (view 28), 1.13 at 39.6 deg. Use a cylindrical strip above 60 deg; label hfov on image and PDF.

parameters.name: origin elevation error to limit error

modules.name: Rooftop and surrounding-building viewpoints
modules.design_question: How do we offer trustworthy views from nearby roofs and rank which ones matter?
modules.method: Vista picks the highest modelled roof triangle (normal Z share at least 0.35), prefers high, broad, central surfaces, lists up to six buildings within 600 m and sets the eye 1.6 m above the roof; its roof heights are OSM-derived and unverified. Upgrade after 30 Nov: (1) roof z from LiDAR-2022 first returns and building-class points per footprint (CGVD28; the portal figure of 0.081 m at 95% does not name roofs, so measure it), shown beside OSM height plus LiDAR ground, footprints-2009 topelev_m (2009, stale) and, outside the City, HRDEM DSM (CGVD2013, about +0.15 m preliminary shift); spread = max minus min; (2) flag appurtenances, which OSM height excludes; (3) rank candidates by elevation angle to the design top, distance, unobstructed ray (BVH) and whether the roof lies inside any cone; (4) a grid index replaces whole-city scans; (5) access stays unknown unless a public viewing roof is listed; (6) never imply a rooftop is an official viewpoint. Output RooftopViewpoint with source, roof z plus or minus spread and building id. Reuse the Vista rooftop self-test (stable building ids restored from the URL hash).

LiDAR-2022 roof z (first returns, building class) per footprint

modules.name: Cone limit estimate, states and exceedance warning
modules.design_question: How do we estimate each cone limit at any point and warn which cone, by how many metres, where, citing the clause and saying it is an estimate?
modules.method: The Guidelines (s.2, p.3) define a cone as two vertical boundaries plus a horizontal lower boundary setting the maximum geodetic height; RTS 16338 Appendix B Table 2 aligns lower boundaries with named reference roofs. Polygons give plan extent only. Hypotheses: H0 flat L per cone (default); H1 historical sheet L = Lv + (Lr - Lv) Dx/Dr, fitted with slope 0 allowed. Tiers: T0 opt-in what-if; T1a published site-vertex limits (2+ sites spanning 30% of the cone, dated after 2024-07-10 or cone absent from Table 2); T1b LiDAR-2022 roof z of the reference building; T2 City data. Plan test: polygon clip in the EPSG:3157 grid with buffer b. Height: e = z_top - L, z orthometric. U95 = k u_c, k = 2 (GUM 6.3.3); fitted limits use Student t. States: outside; near edge; limit unknown; datum unknown; clear (e < -U95); within uncertainty (|e| <= U95); above (e > U95). Overall clear needs every covering cone determinate. Governing cone has the smallest L + U95; the minimum-L cone shows too. The UI says above estimated limit, never violation: clause 3.1.1 is guidance. Hypothetical block: no test until placed; dragging shows live per-cone headroom and a HeadroomMap.
inputs: ConeSet with tier-labelled limit parameters, hypotheses and status
DesignMassing triangles in the EPSG:3157 grid with orthometric z and datum
TerrainSampler (LiDAR-2022) at origin and site (grade)
Reference table of published site limits with approval dates, for calibration
Reference-building roof elevations (LiDAR-2022) for tier T1b
ZoningLimit entered by the designer (optional)
SiteSpec: City parcel, or hypothetical block with placed or unplaced status

Highlighted triangles for the viewer

HeadroomMap: governing limit minus grade per 25 m cell, with a state code; unknown where no limit exists
Card headline: Estimate: above View {view_ref} ({view_name}) limit by {e} m (+/-{U95} m, 95%)
Card second line: {element} at level {z} m {datum}, with a Show me button that flies to the worst point and a section
Expandable detail and PDF: lat, lon, datum, tier, dominant term, status badge, clause 3.1.1 p.6 (guidance wording), Not a City determination; confirm with views@vancouver.ca

parameters.name: L(P)
parameters.relationship: H0: L = L0, constant per cone or sub-cone. H1 (historical): L = Lv + (Lr - Lv) x Dx / Dr, Dx = geodesic distance from view point to site (GeographicLib); fit s with s = 0 allowed.

parameters.name: Hx
parameters.relationship: L(P) - Lbx: maximum height above site grade; LiDAR grade error passes 1:1 into Hx.

parameters.name: e
parameters.relationship: z_top(P) - L(P) at the worst clipped vertex; positive means above the estimated limit; z orthometric in the datum of the limit, never the ENU up axis.

parameters.name: u_c (flat limit)
parameters.relationship: sqrt(u_L^2 + u_grade^2 + u_datum^2); u_grade 0.04 m (0.081 m at 95% divided by 1.96); u_datum 0 for CGVD28 pairs, 0.15 m for CGVD2013, per-origin geoid offset for EGM96; u_L 0.003 m if published.

parameters.name: U95
parameters.relationship: U95 = k u_c; k = 2 (GUM 6.3.3: about 95% if near-normal with many dof); fitted limits use Student t with n - p dof (12.71, 4.30 for 1, 2 dof; GUM Table G.2). Print (95%) beside every +/-.

parameters.name: u_L (tier T1b)
parameters.relationship: Roof-definition ambiguity (parapet, penthouse, pitched facets): 3 m standard uncertainty placeholder from the 1008 Cambie comparison (3.03 m); a rectangular half-width of 3 m would give 1.73 m (GUM 4.3.7). Replace by the measured T1b residual.

parameters.name: U (sloped limit)
parameters.relationship: var L(Dx) = sigma^2 (1/n + (Dx - xbar)^2 / Sxx) from the least-squares fit, which carries the Lv and slope covariance; U95 uses t with n - 2 dof.

parameters.name: state thresholds
parameters.relationship: clear if e < -U95; within uncertainty if |e| <= U95; above if e > U95; ties go to the more cautious state. Example: e = -3.1 m with T1b U95 = 6 m is within uncertainty, not clear.

parameters.name: unknown states
parameters.relationship: Limit unknown: inside plan or buffer, no L at any tier; amber, plan overlap only, prompt to enter or confirm a limit. Datum unknown: relative heights only, exceedance numbers blocked. Neither may ever display as clear.

parameters.name: plan_buffer
parameters.relationship: b = 2 x sqrt(sigma_origin^2 + sigma_hdatum^2 + sigma_footprint^2); defaults 5, 2 and 1 m give 10.95 m; EPSG lists 1.0 m (default) or 2.0 m accuracy for NAD83(CSRS) to WGS 84.

parameters.name: band rule
parameters.relationship: Inside the buffer but outside the polygon, the nearest cone L applies and the card shows the edge distance in metres; near edge with no estimated exceedance is a quiet amber chip, not a full warning.

parameters.name: governing limit
parameters.relationship: L_gov(P) = cone with the smallest L + U95 among cones whose polygon plus buffer contains P; the minimum-L cone is shown when it differs; zoning and ODP heights are not evaluated.

parameters.name: status gate
parameters.relationship: Cones under review (27.1, 27.2) or superseded carry a status badge and Table 1 amendment years in every warning.

parameters.name: tolerance reference
parameters.relationship: 2 m (6.5 ft) appears only as a labelled reference tick tied to clause 3.1.5 wording, never as a pass or fail threshold.

parameters.name: reference caveats
parameters.relationship: G1 and J1 reference anticipated heights; A and 20 lie outside the City; QE views 3.1 and 3.2.4a were deleted in 2024.

parameters.name: hypothetical site
parameters.relationship: SiteSpec block from the brief extract (about 79.2 x 144.8 m, towers 244-305 m, pp.15 and 19) loads from the user own download; no cone test until placed; then the same states apply.

parameters.name: try locations
parameters.relationship: Dragging reruns the check on design triangles only: 0.56 microseconds per triangle, so 50,000 triangles take about 28 ms on the HX laptop; the HeadroomMap is precomputed per limit set.

parameters.name: Buildner question
parameters.relationship: Ask the organisers before the 3 Nov 2026 Q and A deadline whether City view cones bind the hypothetical site; print the answer on the card.

parameters.name: usability test
parameters.relationship: Five entrants place a block, read the card, find the worst point and export the PDF; pass if at least 4 of 5 name the cone, the margin and the estimate status.

modules.name: Skyline comparison and PDF report
modules.design_question: How do we show what the design changes in the existing view and export it as evidence?
modules.method: Render Existing and Proposed from one camera with a wipe slider. Skyline profile: for each azimuth (step 0.1 deg; 0.05 deg for cones narrower than 5 deg) across the cone plus 2 deg each side, march outward over a heightfield and keep the maximum elevation angle; or read the top pixel of each image column. Apply the apparent drop (1-k) d^2/(2R), k = 0.13, to the profile and the render with one function, never to the City limit numbers. Rays = (spread + 4 deg)/step: 56 or 112 for the 1.61 deg cone, 570 or 1,140 for the 53 deg cone. Outputs: three angle arrays, skyline area added (deg^2), share of cone width where the design rises above the existing skyline, margin to the estimated limit line. Keep the Vista report engine; add a vector profile chart, exceedance table with +/-U95, datum line, tier, estimate stamp and a provenance appendix with dataset dates and hashes. Print the context epoch (LiDAR 2022-09, OSM access date, studio-model date) on each image, with a toggle between existing as of 2022 and existing plus pipeline masses. Add alt text, non-colour cues (WCAG 1.4.1) and a live status region (WCAG 4.1.3).
inputs: ViewRender pair: existing and proposed
ContextTiles and TerrainSampler heightfields for the horizon march
ExceedanceReport
Cone boundary azimuths and limit line
Pipeline masses (optional): user-supplied LOD1 with status built after 2022-09, approved or under review
outputs: SkylineProfile arrays and summary numbers
PdfReport: one page per overlapping cone plus summary, clauses and sources
Comparison images with overlays

parameters.name: azimuth_step
parameters.relationship: 0.1 deg default, 0.05 deg for narrow cones; rays = (spread + 4)/step: 56 to 570 at 0.1 deg, 112 to 1,140 at 0.05 deg.

parameters.name: curvature_refraction

modules.name: Design ingest and georeferencing
modules.design_question: How do .3dm, OBJ and IFC models become a placed, mesh-level DesignMassing with an explicit datum?
modules.method: Vista reads .3dm in the browser with rhino3dm (WebAssembly, MIT): meshes, extrusions and brep render meshes, a unit table (mm to yards), caps of 80 MB and 2 M triangles; OBJ is parsed locally; placement puts the model bounding-box base on the terrain at the site; the cone check uses one bounding box per part, which can overestimate. New contract DesignMassing {parts[id, layer, positions Float32, indices Uint32], units, source SHA-256, placement{anchor lat/lon, rotation, base z, datum}}. Placement modes: on site (as Vista), base z from the LiDAR-2022 DTM with its sigma shown; as-modelled coordinates with declared EPSG (EPSG:3157 for Vancouver) and vertical datum; hypothetical block loaded from the user own competition download, unplaced until dropped on the map. Models in true-north axes are rotated by grid convergence (about 0.1 deg: 0.27 m across a 144.8 m block). Vertical datum may be UNKNOWN: view only, exceedance numbers blocked. Layers named mechanical, antenna or mast are flagged appurtenances (clause 3.1.1 includes them). IFC through web-ifc; breps without render meshes are reported, never dropped. Test: the triangle check equals the box check on boxes and is lower on a stepped tower. Nothing is uploaded.

modules.name: AI assistance boundaries and verification gates
modules.design_question: What can GPT-6 Astra and Claude do for this node, and where must survey data and people decide?
modules.method: Allowed, always with a human or deterministic check: code, tests and refactoring of Vista modules; data-cleaning and LiDAR-tile scripts; structuring text already extracted from PDFs into candidate rows (RTS 16338 Table 2, rezoning booklets); reading figures; review of one model work by the other; UI copy written from an ExceedanceReport JSON; fixture generation. Not allowed as a source: terrain, building heights, coordinates, origin elevations, cone parameters or clause text; a reference roof height comes from LiDAR. A 2025 study found coordinate offsets and underestimated elevations in two LLMs. Extraction gate: extract text deterministically first (pypdf extracted the RTS 16338 Table 2 text layer in this round); each model-read number is stored with its page and must pass (a) recomputation by the City formula where possible, (b) a second-model read, (c) a human check against the page; failures never enter ConeSet. Release gate (CI): guidelines.lock.json holds the hand-downloaded 2026 Guidelines SHA-256, retrieval date, signer, pages checked and the 24 Table 1 rows; the build fails if it is missing, unsigned, or a UI clause id is absent from it. Live data is fetched, not recalled. Fetched PDFs and pages are data, not instructions.

flags.claim: Polygon geometry of each cone is enough to estimate maximum building height at every location.
flags.detail: Dataset has no height fields and its coordinates are 2D (verified). A limit needs a geodetic height per cone, from published site limits, reference-building roofs or the City.
flags.correction: Polygons give plan extent only; limits come from tiers T1a, T1b or T2 (M04) with an estimate flag; ask views@vancouver.ca.

flags.claim: The real lower boundary slopes, so a flat ceiling drifts about 36 m per km for every cone.
flags.detail: Guidelines s.2 p.3 say horizontal lower boundary; RTS 16338 Table 2 ties each lower boundary to a reference roof; the slope came from one 1995-99 sheet for old View 9.1.
flags.correction: Per-cone hypotheses: H0 flat (default) and H1 sloped, fitted with s = 0 allowed; the 36 m per km figure is deleted.

flags.claim: Vista frame distances and bearings are correct: Barclay 4.56 km at 347.3 deg; 828 Cambie at 47.14 deg on the cone A edge.
flags.detail: The frame is 0.20% short east-west and 0.58% short north-south. Its 0.08 m footprint residual checks registration to the same transform, not metric accuracy.
flags.correction: GRS80 geodesic: 1060 Barclay 4,596-4,639 m at 346.90-347.24 deg; cone A sector 43.28-47.02 deg; 828 Cambie 1,704.8 m at 47.031 deg, 0.19 m outside.

flags.claim: The 0.56 s check on 1 M triangles was measured on a desktop CPU.
flags.detail: The i7-14650HX is an Intel HX-series laptop processor; thin-and-light student laptops are slower and unmeasured.
flags.correction: Relabelled as a high-end laptop figure; targets are 1 s high-end and 3 s thin laptops, to be measured.

flags.claim: The City 2004 sheet has 6 rows and all were recomputed exactly.
flags.detail: Slide 32 holds about 15 rows, with two reference elevations (485 and 495 ft) at the same Dr, which may indicate sub-cones.
flags.correction: Six rows recompute exactly (validation cases); rows are 1995-99 history, not current parameters; other rows have blank cells in the extract.

flags.claim: No local high-resolution terrain is confirmed; origin elevations must come from SRTM, HRDEM or LidarBC.
flags.detail: City LiDAR 2022 covers the City and UBC at about 49 pts/m2 (0.081 m at 95%), CGVD28GVRD; the 17 origins lie in 11 tiles, all confirmed present.
flags.correction: LiDAR-2022 is the primary source for origin z, grade and roofs; HRDEM and SRTM serve only the North Shore backdrop.

flags.claim: Footprints-2009 elevations have no stated datum.
flags.detail: The portal describes TOPELEV_M and BASEELEV_M as geodetic metres; the datum itself is still not named.
flags.correction: Record geodetic, likely CGVD28 (unconfirmed); 2009-era and approximate, so a third source in the roof spread.

flags.claim: A far plane of 8 km is enough for the camera rig.
flags.detail: Named subjects lie 12.5-24.6 km from the origins; the Vista observer camera already uses 45,000 m.
flags.correction: Far plane at least 60 km with reversed-Z or log depth; test that every Table 1 subject renders.

flags.claim: SRTM is accurate enough for origin elevations.
flags.detail: USGS gives 16 m linear error at 90% (about 10 m actual), measured to the canopy top; under H1 an origin error can reach the limit 1:1.
flags.correction: Use LiDAR-2022 for origins; keep SRTM only as a distant backdrop fallback.

flags.claim: A single flat study ceiling is a useful stand-in for a cone.
flags.detail: The City model is one horizontal geodetic height per cone or sub-cone, not one ceiling for all cones; some cones may also carry sub-cones or view shadows.
flags.correction: Keep the user ceiling only as a labelled what-if (T0); default to a per-cone limit with its tier.

flags.claim: The polygon apex equals the by-law origin point (Vista).
flags.detail: 16 apexes match 16 origin points and the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m, but no survey check exists; open-data text for 9.1 and 9.2 names the older origin.

flags.claim: Eye height is 1.6 m.
flags.detail: No City eye height found; a 5 ft 6 in average-person reference (stature, not eye height) appears in a City Q and A snippet. Keep editable and labelled.

flags.claim: Vertical datum of the City geodetic cone heights.
flags.detail: CGVD28 is likely: BC legal surveys use it (LTSA 465C) and LiDAR-2022 is CGVD28GVRD. A search snippet shows CD-1 by-laws define Geodetic Datum as the City reference surface without naming it.

flags.claim: Which Trout Lake geometry (27.1, 27.2) is in force, and which subject each carries.
flags.detail: City report of 2026-06-23 calls 27.1 the existing cone with updates under review. Table 1 (Jul 2024, Jun 2025) gives 27.1 North Shore Mountains, 27.2 Lions; open data and Vista say 27.1 is the Lions.

flags.claim: Whether the open-data apexes for 9.1 and 9.2 match the amended origin.
flags.detail: The Vista extract of the 2026 Table 1 says base of the City Hall stairs; the Jun 2025 Table 1 and open-data descriptions say Walking Figures plaza.

flags.claim: Guidelines clause text, page numbers and rezoning figures.
flags.detail: Text read in Jul 2024 and Jun 2025 copies of unverified provenance; the 2026-02-04 text and rezoning booklets returned HTTP 403 again on 2026-10-21; booklet numbers come from search summaries.

flags.claim: One horizontal plane per view describes the City limit.
flags.detail: Table 2 shows lower boundaries shared between views (G1.2, J1.1) and anticipated heights; the 2004 slides mention sub-cones and view shadow. Test piecewise and multi-reference models.

flags.claim: The roof of the named reference building sets the horizontal limit.
flags.detail: Reading of RTS 16338 Table 2 plus s.2 p.3; footprints-2009 puts the 1008 Cambie tower at 102.68 m against 105.71 m published for cone A. LiDAR-2022 test pending.

flags.claim: Vista code and data packs can be reused openly.
flags.detail: None of the four repos has a LICENSE file; the pack derives from a studio-supplied model plus OSM (ODbL); Form Studio omitted the competition model for ownership. Add MIT or Apache; rebuild packs.

flags.claim: Buildner policy on AI-generated images in entries.
flags.detail: r2: FAQ and terms read; AI images are not banned and the terms are silent on AI (see r2 flag). The Brief itself was not read, so a brief-level AI or software rule is unconfirmed.

flags.claim: GPT-6 Astra reads images and PDFs reliably.
flags.detail: OpenAI model page lists image input and text output; PDF file input is not listed, though the PDF guide says vision-capable models accept PDFs. Reliability on tables is untested; RTS 16338 has a text layer, so extract text first.

flags.claim: Student laptops meet 5 MB, 30 fps and 500 MB targets.
flags.detail: No device survey; the 0.56 s check ran on one HX-series laptop CPU. Test on three laptop classes.

flags.claim: OSM heights are good enough for rooftop views.
flags.detail: OSM height excludes antennas and spires, but the City counts appurtenances; 4,800 of 9,897 studio-model heights are type estimates. LiDAR-2022 roofs replace them where present.

flags.claim: Default plan buffer and uncertainty values.
flags.detail: sigma_origin 5 m, sigma_hdatum 2 m and sigma_footprint 1 m are placeholders; EPSG lists 1.0 m or 2.0 m accuracy for NAD83(CSRS) to WGS 84 but the offset is not computed; LiDAR sigma is 0.081/1.96 assuming normal errors.

flags.claim: Status of view 12.2 (Granville Bridge).
flags.detail: Jul 2024 Table 1 lists 12.2 (Mount Seymour); Jun 2025 Table 1 omits it though clause 3.4.2 still names it; open data has no polygon for it.

flags.claim: A UTM 10 grid agrees with the Vincenty GRS80 inverse within 0.1 m and 0.01 deg on QE to Barclay, so EPSG:3157 kernels meet 0.05 m and 0.001 deg.
flags.detail: Grid distance carries scale 0.99960 and grid bearing carries convergence (-0.085 deg at QE): 4,637.11 m at 346.986 deg against geodesic 4,638.97 m at 346.900 deg. Worst of 50 cone edges: 2.48 m, 0.105 deg.
flags.correction: Run containment wholly in the grid; take reported distances and azimuths from GeographicLib; never mix. After mean-scale and convergence correction the grid matches the geodesic within 0.0001 m and 0.0001 deg.

flags.claim: LiDAR-2022 accuracy is 0.081 m at 95% on open ground.
flags.detail: The portal says vertical accuracy 0.081 metre (95% confidence level) and names no land cover and no standard. Roof and edge accuracy is not stated.
flags.correction: Write 0.081 m at 95% (land cover and standard not stated); measure roof z against reference points before relying on sub-metre roof limits.

flags.claim: The Buildner answer on AI-generated images is unread and unknown.
flags.detail: The FAQ is readable: check the AI tool terms; AI images are not recommended as sole work. Terms 4.1-4.4 ask for original work and image licences on request and do not mention AI.
flags.correction: AI images are not banned; record the tool and its terms. The Brief itself (email sign-up) is still unread.

flags.claim: First-user designs sit on real downtown sites, where the cone test applies directly.
flags.detail: The brief extract describes a hypothetical full-block site of about 79.2 x 144.8 m (p.15) and towers of 244-305 m (p.19). The Buildner page and terms name neither view cones nor the Guidelines.
flags.correction: Entrant checks are what-if location studies: hypothetical-site mode, live headroom while dragging, a HeadroomMap, and a Buildner Q and A question before 3 Nov.

flags.claim: A per-cone ENU frame can replace EPSG:3157 for the exceedance test.
flags.detail: An ENU up axis departs from orthometric height by d^2/2R: 0.23 m at 1.7 km, 1.66 m at 4.6 km, 2.83 m at 6 km, far above u_L = 0.003 m for a published limit.
flags.correction: Plan coordinates in EPSG:3157; z always orthometric in the datum of the limit; ENU only as a render frame with the shared drop function.

flags.claim: Whether City view cones bind the hypothetical Tall Challenge site.
flags.detail: The brief asks for 244-305 m towers; published limits found are 105.71 m (cone A) and 123.201 m (3.2.1), both unverified summaries. The brief PDF needs an email sign-up and was not read.

flags.claim: Edge convention of the City cone polygons.
flags.detail: Cone A east edge: straight in lon/lat deviates 0.22 m from the geodesic at 3 km; grid-straight 0.0002 m. 828 Cambie reads 0.19 m outside or 0.02 m inside by convention.

flags.claim: Vista fog hides the North Shore peaks.
flags.detail: explorer.js line 410: context fog far 9,000 m; line 433: backdrop pass 42,000 m, giving 4.9% haze at 12.5 km and 18.9% at 24.6 km (default style). Vista was not executed; the visual result is untested.

flags.claim: Reversed-Z (reversedDepthBuffer) works on student laptops.
flags.detail: Khronos lists EXT_clip_control as Community Approved (2023-11-02) with no support list; three.js states the requirement. Safari and integrated-GPU support is unknown.
flags.correction: Detect at runtime, fall back to logarithmic depth, log the path on every camera record.

flags.claim: An 11.5 person-day MVP fits the 23 days to 13 Nov 2026.
flags.detail: Capacity of two students with other studio work is unknown; MVP shares of module efforts are team estimates.

flags.claim: U95 states use k = 2 and a 3 m T1b placeholder.
flags.detail: k = 2 assumes near-normal errors; 3 m taken as one standard uncertainty is conservative (1.73 m if a rectangular half-width); thresholds change once the T1b residual is measured.
